implementation: The public Doc printer accepts DocumentSyntax, PrintMode and explicit guest bindings/texts. It returns a source artifact with the exact entry category, typed invalid input, or a stopped result under the same operation budget.

Prefix covers 20 categories and 64 forms. Compact uses a sentence literal only for representable Text/Concat/Ruby/Anno content. Break, formatting and foreign content preserve their explicit semantic constructors.
The three standalone guest entries and four language wrappers retain ForeignClosure, owner environment, source/view/origin identity and guest syntax without implicit semantic evaluation.

Source-less names and language spellings use the shared lexical contract. Unprintable values return typed failures instead of replacement text. Iterative traversal charges work, nodes, allocation, depth, source admission and output before producing data.

PrintedGuest is an explicit host assertion. Canonical document and guest digests bind its target, not the correctness of its text. The public suite must validate actual guest syntax/source correspondence before claiming a normal roundtrip. It must not require semantic success for Code examples.
The request/reply schema and first CBOR boundary validate the owned source closure, IDs, exact digest lengths and report invariants without using ambient source records.

independent_review.scope: Fixed Doc printer 28 + contracts1 only; excludes RegionQuery and Custom map ownership work.
independent_review.managed: 7 actual printer tests pass on native and WASI, including 64 forms x Prefix/Compact and 6 guest fragments. Root full workspace/quality gates recorded separately.
independent_review.findings: No blocking finding. Three independent programs pass on native and WASI: original-source roundtrips, genuine engine-printer guest inputs and independently constructed digest expectations, alias/assertion boundaries, six resource limits, source admission once, caller depth, cancellation and source-less values. Same-identity invalid guest text is deliberately shown to assemble but fail actual parsing, documenting the low-level host-assertion boundary.

log_normalization: Root logs use LF and a final newline. Archived independent UTF-8 records preserve original bytes and SHA-256.
